title: Chapter 40 — Midnight, Forecastle
paragraphs: HARPOONERS AND SAILORS.
(The foresail rises and reveals the watch standing, lounging, leaning, and lying in various positions, all singing in chorus.)
Farewell and goodbye to you, Spanish ladies! Farewell and goodbye to you, ladies of Spain! Our captain's commanded —
1ST NANTUCKET SAILOR. Oh, boys, don't be sentimental — it's bad for the digestion! Take a tonic, follow me!
(Sings, and all follow.)

Our captain stood upon the deck, A spyglass in his hand, Surveying those gallant whales That blew at every strand. Oh, your tubs in your boats, my boys, And by your braces stand, And we'll have one of those fine whales, Hand, boys, over hand! So, be cheery, my lads! May your hearts never fail! While the bold harpooner is striking the whale!
MATE'S VOICE FROM THE QUARTER-DECK. Eight bells there, forward!

2ND NANTUCKET SAILOR. Stop the chorus! Eight bells there! Do you hear, bell-boy? Strike the bell eight, you Pip! You blackling! And let me call the watch. I've got the right kind of mouth for that — the hogshead mouth. So, so — (Thrusts his head down the hatch.) Star-bo-l-e-e-n-s, a-h-o-y! Eight bells there below! Tumble up!

DUTCH SAILOR. Great sleeping tonight, mate — a fat night for it. I notice this about our old Mogul's wine: it deadens some just as much as it livens up others. We sing, they sleep — yes, lying down there like the bottom tier of casks in the hold. At them again! Here, take this copper pump and hail them through it. Tell them to stop dreaming about their girls. Tell them it's the resurrection — they must give their last kiss and come to judgment. That's the way — that's it! Your throat hasn't been ruined by eating Amsterdam butter.

FRENCH SAILOR. Listen, boys! Let's have a jig or two before we anchor in Blanket Bay. What do you say? Here comes the other watch. Everybody on your feet! Pip! Little Pip! Come on with your tambourine!
PIP. (Sulky and sleepy.) Don't know where it is.

FRENCH SAILOR. Beat your belly, then, and flap your ears. Dance, men, I say! Merry's the word — hurrah! Damn me, won't you dance? Line up, Indian file, and gallop into the double-shuffle! Throw yourselves into it! Legs! Legs!
ICELAND SAILOR. I don't like your floor, mate — it's too springy for my taste. I'm used to ice floors. I'm sorry to throw cold water on the subject, but excuse me.
MALTESE SAILOR. Me too. Where are your girls? Who but a fool would take his own left hand in his right and say, 'How do you do?' Partners! I need partners!
SICILIAN SAILOR. That's right — girls and a green lawn! Then I'll dance with you — yes, I'll leap like a grasshopper!
LONG-ISLAND SAILOR. Well, well, you sulkers, there's plenty more of us. Hoe corn while you can, I say. All legs go to the harvest soon enough. Ah! Here comes the music — now for it!

AZORE SAILOR. (Climbing up and tossing the tambourine through the hatch.) Here you go, Pip — and there's the windlass post. Climb up! Now, boys! (Half of them dance to the tambourine; some go below; some sleep or lie among the coils of rigging. Plenty of cursing.)
AZORE SAILOR. (Dancing.) Go it, Pip! Bang it, bell-boy! Rig it, dig it, stig it, quig it, bell-boy! Make fireflies! Break the jinglers!
PIP. Jinglers, you say? There goes another one — fell off. I'm pounding it too hard.
CHINA SAILOR. Rattle your teeth, then, and keep pounding — make a pagoda of yourself.
FRENCH SAILOR. Wild and merry! Hold up your hoop, Pip, so I can jump through it! Split jibs! Tear yourselves!
TASHTEGO. (Quietly smoking.) That's a white man for you. He calls that fun. Humph! I'll save my sweat.

OLD MANX SAILOR. I wonder whether those cheerful lads realize what they're dancing over. 'I'll dance over your grave, I will' — that's the bitterest threat of your night-women, the ones who beat headwinds around corners. O Christ! To think of the green navies and the green-skulled crews! Well, well — maybe the whole world is a ball, as you scholars have it, and so it's only right to make one ballroom of it. Dance on, lads — you're young. I was once.
3RD NANTUCKET SAILOR. Break time! Whew! This is harder work than rowing after whales in a calm. Give us a puff, Tash.
(They stop dancing and gather in groups. Meanwhile, the sky darkens — the wind rises.)
LASCAR SAILOR. By Brahma! Boys, it'll be time to douse sail soon. The heaven-born, high-tide Ganges has turned to wind! You show your black brow, Seeva!

MALTESE SAILOR. (Reclining and shaking his cap.) It's the waves — the whitecaps are dancing now. They'll shake their tassels soon. If only all the waves were women — then I'd gladly go drown, and dance with them forever! There's nothing so sweet on earth — heaven itself can't match it — as those swift glances from warm, wild women's bosoms in the dance, when their arching arms hide such ripe, bursting grapes.

SICILIAN SAILOR. (Reclining.) Don't tell me about it! Listen, lad — fleet interlacings of the limbs — lithe swayings — coyings — flutterings! Lip! Heart! Hip! All graze: unceasing touch and go! Not a taste, mind you, or else satiety sets in. Eh, Pagan? (Nudging.)

TAHITIAN SAILOR. (Reclining on a mat.) Hail, holy nakedness of our dancing girls — the Heeva-Heeva! Ah, low-veiled, palm-crowned Tahiti! I still rest on your mat, but the soft earth has shifted! I saw you woven in the forest, my mat! Green the first day I carried you home; now worn and wilted. Ah me! Neither you nor I can bear the change! How would it be, then, if transplanted to that sky? Can I hear the roaring streams from Pirohitee's peak of spears, when they leap down the cliffs and drown the villages? — The blast! The blast! Up, spine, and face it! (Leaps to his feet.)
PORTUGUESE SAILOR. How the sea crashes against the hull! Stand by for reefing, lads! The winds are just crossing swords — soon they'll go lunging at each other.

DANISH SAILOR. Crack, crack, old ship! As long as you're cracking, you're holding! Well done! The mate keeps you to it firmly. He's no more afraid than the island fortress at Kattegat, built to fight the Baltic with storm-battered guns, crusted with sea salt!
4TH NANTUCKET SAILOR. He has his orders, mind you. I heard old Ahab tell him he must always kill a squall, the way you burst a waterspout with a pistol — fire your ship right into it!
ENGLISH SAILOR. Bloody hell, but that old man's a grand old fellow! We're the lads to hunt up his whale!
ALL. Yes! Yes!

OLD MANX SAILOR. How the three pines — the masts — shake! Pines are the hardest sort of tree to keep alive when moved to any other soil, and here there's none but the crew's cursed clay. Steady, helmsman! Steady. This is the sort of weather when brave hearts snap ashore, and keeled hulls split at sea. Our captain has his birthmark. Look there, boys — there's another one in the sky — lurid-like, you see, and all else pitch black.
DAGGOO. What of that? Whoever's afraid of black is afraid of me! I'm quarried out of it!

SPANISH SAILOR. (Aside.) He wants a fight, does he? The old grudge makes me touchy. (Stepping forward.) Yes, harpooner, your race is the undeniable dark side of mankind — devilishly dark, at that. No offense.
DAGGOO. (Grimly.) None.
ST. JAGO'S SAILOR. That Spaniard is either mad or drunk. But it can't be drink, or else in his one case our old Mogul's firewater is rather slow in working.
5TH NANTUCKET SAILOR. What's that I see — lightning? Yes.
SPANISH SAILOR. No. Daggoo showing his teeth.
DAGGOO. (Springing forward.) Swallow yours, runt! White skin, white liver!
SPANISH SAILOR. (Meeting him.) I'll carve you up! Big body, small soul!
ALL. A fight! A fight! A fight!
TASHTEGO. (Taking a puff.) A fight below and a fight aloft — gods and men, both brawlers! Humph!
BELFAST SAILOR. A fight! Arrah, a fight! The Virgin be blessed, a fight! Dive right in!
ENGLISH SAILOR. Fair play! Grab the Spaniard's knife! Make a ring, a ring!
OLD MANX SAILOR. Already formed — look! The ringed horizon. In that ring, Cain struck Abel. Sweet work, proper work! No? Then why, God, did you make the ring?
MATE'S VOICE FROM THE QUARTER-DECK. Hands to the halyards! Take in topgallant sails! Stand by to reef topsails!
ALL. The squall! The squall! Jump, my jollies! (They scatter.)

PIP. (Shrinking under the windlass.) Jollies? Lord help such jollies! Crish, crash! There goes the jib-stay! Blang-whang! God! Duck lower, Pip — here comes the royal yard! It's worse than being in the whirled woods on the last day of the year! Who'd go climbing after chestnuts now? But there they go, all cursing, and here I don't. Fine prospects to them — they're on the road to heaven. Hold on tight! Jiminy, what a squall! But those fellows there are worse yet — they are your white squalls, they are. White squalls? White whale, shh! Shh! Here I've heard all their talk just now, and the white whale — shh! Shh! — spoken of only once! And only this evening — it makes me jingle all over like my tambourine — that anaconda of an old man swore them in to hunt him! Oh, you big white God up there somewhere in that darkness, have mercy on this small black boy down here. Preserve him from all men who have no guts to feel fear!
